A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same offline-to-online RL research, with matching Cal-QL/IQL instantiations, datasets, and diffusion formulations despite substantial revision and renaming. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original D4RL evaluations, learning curves, and ablations, including Table 1 and Appendices C–H.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, behavioral diagnostics, and controlled experiments, including Tables 1–3 and Appendices D–I.

M1.justification: V1's KL-score sorting into fixed-ratio subsets becomes L2 behavioral distance with Gaussian-posterior thresholds and a sign-based exchange rule in v2. DARE also permits an online-policy behavioral reference and specifies separate PEX/SAC actor objectives for its IQL instantiation. These change the reported procedure beyond renaming StratDiff.

E1.justification: V2 retains the nine locomotion and four AntMaze tasks, adds AntMaze large-diverse and large-play, and evaluates four Adroit human-v0 manipulation tasks. Adroit introduces a distinct contact-rich manipulation domain absent from v1.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds plain CQL as a separate comparator alongside Cal-QL and EDIS-C, and adds PEX alongside IQL and EDIS-I. This substantially broadens the central comparisons with backbone and online-adaptation controls. EDIS-C/EDIS-I correspond to the earlier EDIS variants, rather than additional methods created by renaming.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled protocols varying online objectives and behavioral references, reversed assignment capped at 32 exchanges, and an overlap diagnostic using a 100,000-transition online buffer. V1's UTD=1 versus 10 experiment at 0.12M steps and fixed exchange-cap experiments are removed. The principal 1M offline/0.2M online budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds posterior-versus-Gaussian/direct exchange comparisons, alternative behavior-model and objective tests, reversed assignment, and behavioral-overlap/statistics diagnostics. Exchange-removal ablations and exchange-count analyses are revised and expanded. V1's energy-removal, expectile-loss, UTD, and exchange-cap sensitivity studies are absent from v2.

E5.justification: V2 newly specifies aggregation over the final four evaluations as well as five random seeds in Table 1 and Appendix C; v1 specifies only five-seed averaging. Both retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. The added aggregation specification does not establish an increased number of independent runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises many retained-task results: Cal-QL on H-MR changes from 66.8±40.5 to 93.0±13.4, while the proposed Cal-QL variant on HC-MR changes from 62.3±2.4 to 77.6±2.6. V2 also adds large-AntMaze, Adroit, offline-initialization, and new diagnostic results. Method revisions and newly specified aggregation prevent interpreting the proposed-method differences as established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's cited CEP theorem, v2 introduces likelihood-ratio sufficiency assumptions, Gaussian posterior geometry, exchange thresholds, mean-separation analysis, and an asserted threshold-class H∆H-divergence guarantee, with proofs in Appendix A. The existing diffusion derivations are largely retained in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The core contribution shifts from energy-guided diffusion stratification to a general framework for sample-level constraint release. V2 adds claims of behavior-model and algorithm independence, novelty of posterior-induced release, and provable behavioral separation. These substantially broaden and redefine the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: V1 presents energy guidance as essential; v2 treats diffusion as optional and attributes effectiveness to posterior geometry and behavior-consistent assignment. V2 adds task- and initialization-dependent objective interpretations, Gaussian-approximation qualifications, and computational tradeoffs for policy references. V1's explicit diffusion-quality, guidance-scale, and fixed-ratio limitations are no longer presented.

D1.justification: V2 documents moment estimation every 1,000 steps using 10,000 samples per source, SAC entropy coefficients, shared initializations, and detailed EDIS settings. Conversely, v1's diffusion-training budget, architecture, and energy-network specifications are omitted. The code statement changes from future release upon acceptance to an included supplementary archive; actual archive availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Related work is substantively reorganized around constraint handling and behavioral alignment instead of diffusion-centered positioning. V2 adds discussions of Uni-RL and OPT, the proper policy-expansion reference, and domain-adaptation theory supporting its divergence analysis. Its distinction from prior work now emphasizes behavioral rather than origin-based constraint assignment.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves earlier, motivation becomes a separate section, instantiations are separated from the general framework, and an appendix guide is added. This is substantial narrative restructuring alongside the scientific changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, removes the original framework schematic, and replaces the motivation histograms with overlap visualizations. It adds posterior-geometry and statistics plots, expands Table 1's comparator/task structure, and adds several experimental displays. Main learning curves move to the appendix, while exchange analyses receive redesigned combined plots.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through broader benchmarks, additional baselines, and targeted mechanism controls. However, its new central theoretical guarantee is false as stated: under Appendix A's definitions, exchanging 2 and 3 between B0={0,2,6} and B1={0,3,4} satisfies the exchange rule but reduces threshold-class H∆H divergence from 4/3 to 2/3, contradicting Theorem 4. The substantial empirical benefits therefore coexist with a substantive new theoretical reliability problem, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
